clue.text: Second merchant doesn't finish wine

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: the trader's word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a seller is one who trades goods

explanation.surface: A trader of the second rank fails to complete his wine sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't finish' drops the last letter of SELLER, leaving SELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the valley of the river of that name in Germany.

clue.text: It darkens fringes of a woman's outlook on things

definitions.text: It darkens fringes of a woman's outlook on things

parts.words: It darkens fringes of a woman's outlook on things
parts.note: the fringes are eyelashes, the edges of the eyes she looks out through

explanation.surface: Something that casts gloom on a woman's view of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringes' are eyelashes and 'outlook' is the eyes, not her attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is cosmetic used to darken and thicken eyelashes.

clue.text: Racing around oarsman in small republic

indicators.note: racing around suggests letters dashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: Crews rowing about a rower in a tiny state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racing around' rearranges the letters of OARSMAN IN.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Machine makes one nearly sweat

indicators.note: nearly means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: lather is froth of sweat, as on a horse

explanation.surface: A machine that leaves you almost in a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter of LATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that turns a workpiece against a cutter.

clue.text: Made ready?

parts.note: 'ready' is slang for cash (ready money), so made money; past tense of gaining wages

explanation.surface: Something prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for cash, so 'made ready' means got money.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gained money by work is to have got pay; 'ready' is slang for cash.

clue.text: Follow and prosper

explanation.surface: Two verbs for coming after and doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after someone in office is to succeed them; to thrive in a venture is also to succeed.

clue.text: It's more detestable when hooter's used

definitions.text: It's more detestable when hooter's used

parts.words: It's more detestable when hooter's used
parts.note: the hooter is the nose, so something more offensive to the nose

explanation.surface: A car horn makes something even more hateful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' is slang for nose, not a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a stronger odour is more offensive to the nose.

clue.text: Look around inside cooked chapati for a sausage

indicators.note: inside places the turned word within the cooked flatbread letters
cooked signals the flatbread's letters are reworked
around turns the word for look backwards

parts.note: lo means look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Peering into a cooked flatbread in search of a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns LO into OL; 'cooked' rearranges CHAPATI to CHIPATA; 'inside' places OL within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage.

clue.text: Chemical damaged trees

indicators.note: damaged suggests the tree letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Chemical damage to trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Piece of furniture helps actor get ready

explanation.surface: Someone helps an actor prepare, perhaps at a sideboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a kitchen sideboard with shelves; in theatre a dresser is the assistant who helps a performer into costume.

clue.text: Politician takes Japanese money to register returns

parts.note: the sen is a small Japanese coin, a hundredth of a yen

indicators.note: the roster word comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a rota is a list or roster of names

explanation.surface: A politician pockets yen and goes back to sign in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of an upper legislative house, a lawmaker.

clue.text: I sleep, taking time to rewrite long letter

indicators.note: to rewrite here means the given letters are written out in a new order

explanation.surface: A sleepy writer naps before redrafting a lengthy letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rewrite' rearranges ISLEEP plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or lengthy letter, like those of the New Testament.

clue.text: What Venus de Milo might have said? How novel!

definitions.text: What Venus de Milo might have said? How novel!

parts.words: What Venus de Milo might have said? How novel!
parts.note: the armless statue might bid goodbye to her limbs; the phrase is also the title of a Hemingway novel

explanation.surface: Imagining the armless statue's parting words, and admiring the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo is a famous ancient Greek statue missing both arms. The title is Hemingway's 1929 war novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a goodbye to one's limbs and the title of Ernest Hemingway's novel.

clue.text: Thin plate around creature

indicators.note: around signals the plate word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or plate

explanation.surface: A thin metal sheet wrapped round some beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns LAMINA back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living creature is an animal.

clue.text: Birdie? Better than that!

parts.note: in golf a birdie is one under par; a score three under is better, and is also named after a seabird

explanation.surface: A golfer's score, and something better still.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf scores under par are named after birds: birdie (one under), eagle (two), and this (three).
explanation.definitionFit: In golf this is three under par on a hole, a better score than a birdie; it is also a large seabird.

clue.text: 12 is unable to fit in bottle

indicators.note: to fit in tells us the inability word is placed within the creature

parts.note: 12-across is a creature, and a deer is one
can't means is unable

explanation.surface: An animal too large to squeeze into a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' refers to the answer of 12-across, which is a creature, here a DEER; 'to fit in' places CANT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel, a stoppered bottle for serving wine.

clue.text: It's just like a T-Rex to be appetising

explanation.surface: A dinosaur with an appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the word literally as 'having many teeth', as the dinosaur does.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrannosaurus is full of teeth, and in its usual sense the word means tasty or delicious.

clue.text: Asian relation touring

indicators.note: touring suggests letters travelling around into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative travelling around Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' rearranges RELATION. The answer is printed ORIENTAI, an OCR slip for ORIENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental is a dated word for something from the East, Asian.

clue.text: We hear they're prized as openers!

definitions.text: We hear they're prized as openers!

parts.words: We hear they're prized as openers!
parts.note: prized sounds like prised: these iron levers are used to prise things open

explanation.surface: Something valued as an opener, perhaps a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prized' read by sound is 'prised', forced open with a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowbars are iron levers used for prising lids and doors open.

clue.text: Primrose threatens with impudent talk

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate or threaten them
lip is cheek, insolent backchat

explanation.surface: A girl called Primrose bullies people with her cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primrose' looks like a name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild flower of the primula genus, a kind of primrose.

clue.text: A party on opening Western temple? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading from right to left
quite the opposite tells us the stated order is to be flipped round

parts.note: a do is a party
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: A celebration at the opening of a temple in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: A + DO + GAP gives ADOGAP; 'Western' and 'Quite the opposite' turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in Asia.

clue.text: Checks collars

explanation.surface: Police checks and arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt a process is to arrest it, and to collar a suspect is to take them into custody.

clue.text: One's going to court around Circle Line

parts.note: I for one plus 's, giving one is
the round letter O stands for around
the bar is the court, as in being called to the Bar

explanation.surface: Someone is off to court via a London Underground line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it means a line forming a ring, as isobars on weather maps do round highs and lows.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobars on weather maps are lines of equal pressure that often form closed rings.

clue.text: Painting of birds by a lepidopterist?

parts.note: whistlers are birds, a family of Australasian songbirds
a lepidopterist studies moths, so might be called a 'mother', one who moths

explanation.surface: A butterfly collector's picture of some songbirds.
explanation.walkthrough: The painting is James McNeill Whistler's portrait of his mother; 'mother' is read as one who hunts moths.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the popular name for Whistler's 1871 portrait of his mother, a famous painting.

clue.text: Champion missing wide part of target

indicators.note: missing means the wide letter is lost

parts.note: a winner is a champion
W is the cricket abbreviation for wide

explanation.surface: A champion archer misses wide of the target.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring of a target next to the bullseye.

clue.text: Work on spasmodic moment of vision

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tic is a sudden involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Work on a sudden twitch in someone's eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective relating to the eye and sight.

clue.text: Ruffian's entertaining in European Rugby move

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, as a host has guests in

parts.note: a lout is a ruffian; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A thug hosting a European visitor during a rugby game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' places IN and E inside LOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-out is the restart in rugby union when the ball is thrown in between two lines of forwards.

clue.text: They secure pantomime page boy

explanation.surface: Security for a pantomime character.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons fasten clothes; Buttons is also the page boy in the Cinderella pantomime, a British Christmas stage show.

clue.text: Soldiers look around in the shade

parts.note: paras are paratroopers, soldiers

indicators.note: around turns the word for look about, read backwards

parts.note: lo means look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Troops glance about while resting in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns LO into OL. The answer is printed PARASOI, an OCR slip for PARASOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, an umbrella giving shade from the sun.

clue.text: Insects don't start disease

indicators.note: don't start means the insects lose their first letter

parts.note: crickets are chirping insects

explanation.surface: Insects free from disease, so long as they don't begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a bone-softening illness caused by lack of vitamin D.
